did_you_know.text: Did you know? Sheba son of Bichri is described as a “worthless man” and a “Benjamite,” meaning he was from the tribe of Benjamin. He led a revolt against David by calling out, “We have no share in David.”
Did you know? Following Sheba’s call, all the men of Israel deserted David, while the men of Judah remained loyal to him, “from the Jordan to Jerusalem.”

Did you know? After returning to Jerusalem, David took the ten concubines he had left to look after the palace and placed them under guard. He provided for them but no longer slept with them, and they remained secluded until the day they died.
Did you know? David appointed Amasa to mobilize the men of Judah within three days, but Amasa delayed and did not meet the deadline David had given him.

Did you know? David viewed Sheba son of Bichri’s revolt as a serious threat. He even told Abishai that Sheba might cause them more harm than Absalom had, so he ordered him to pursue Sheba before he could retreat into fortified cities.

Did you know? Joab killed Amasa during what initially appeared to be a friendly meeting. He said to him, “Are you well, my brother?” and asked to kiss him, but Amasa did not notice the sword in Joab’s hand.
Did you know? Sheba son of Bichri fled to Abel Beth Maakah, where Joab laid siege to the city. Joab’s men built a siege ramp against the city and tried to bring down the wall.
Did you know? It was a wise woman from the city who took the initiative to negotiate with Joab and asked him to listen to what she had to say, attempting to save the entire city.
Did you know? Joab did not seek to destroy Abel Beth Maakah. He demanded only one person be handed over to him: Sheba son of Bichri, who had rebelled against King David.
Did you know? The wise woman persuaded the people of the city, and they cut off Sheba’s head and threw it to Joab. As a result, Joab blew the trumpet, and the army withdrew from the city.
